learning: Hypotheses: (1) line loss on the s-bend and slalom is a turning-authority limit, so a narrower track should clear it; (2) max_error should fall below 0.06 on the bends once line loss clears; (3) steering_oscillation may rise modestly with the narrower track, and kd 0.4 should still damp it. The oval finish rate (0.75 at iteration 4) checks that the working configuration is preserved. Report completion_time for any finished run so base_speed can be judged later.
notes: Restores the iteration-4 controller and sensor layout and changes only wheel_track to 0.10 m, as the Builder proposed. Single-variable change so the race result can be attributed to track width. Adds noise_robustness to the measurement request.
rationale: Iteration 4 (50 mm span at x = ±0.025 m, y = 0.075 m, sensor_size 0.012 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, kd 0.4) is the best design so far at 291.9. The oval finished 15 of 20 runs, but the s-bend and slalom still lost the line in every run, with line_loss_events at 2.0 on both and max_error at 0.072 and 0.066. Iterations 5 and 6 both tested wider or larger sensing and both hurt the oval: a 60 mm span dropped it to 0 of 20 (score 73.6), and a 16 mm footprint at 50 mm also dropped it to 0 of 20 (score 83.5). The Builder's proposal restores the iteration-4 geometry and changes only wheel_track, from 0.12 m to 0.10 m. A narrower track raises turn rate for the same wheel-command difference (turn rate = wheel speed difference / wheel_track), which targets the remaining line loss on the bends, which is consistent with a turning-authority limit. I keep the controller identical to iteration 4 (base_speed 1.4, kp 4.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.4, last_direction, weights [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1]) so the track width is the only variable that moves and the result can be attributed to it. kd 0.4 is retained because it brought steering_oscillation down to 0.16 on the oval. Expected result: line_loss_events below 2.0 on the s-bend and slalom, max_error below 0.06 on some bends, and the oval finish rate holding near 0.75. Risk: a narrower track can raise steering_oscillation, which is the watch point. If the oval finish rate drops sharply, the Builder's plan is to revert wheel_track to 0.12 m.
